patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a simplified stacked layout with no visible horizontal navigation links, while the desktop sketch clearly shows a full top navigation bar. This responsive reduction strongly implies a mobile nav toggle that reveals hidden navigation.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A hamburger button should open and close a navigation drawer or overlay containing the primary site links. It should update expanded state and likely lock background scroll while open.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly draw the hamburger icon or the opened menu state, so the exact panel style (drawer, dropdown, fullscreen overlay) is inferred from the desktop/mobile contrast.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The inferred mobile navigation drawer/toggle requires keyboard-operable state changes and controlled focus movement. Desktop navigation also needs logical keyboard traversal across top-level links.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: When the mobile menu opens, focus should move into it and return to the trigger on close. Keyboard navigation order should remain logical across nav, map CTA, and footer links.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit modal or disclosure states are drawn; focus handling is inferred from the presence of interactive navigation and CTA elements.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a mostly static informational site with low JavaScript complexity. The main cross-viewport interaction difference is navigation: desktop presents a visible horizontal nav, while mobile likely collapses that navigation behind a hamburger-controlled panel. No forms, tabs, accordions, infinite loading, or modal content are suggested by the drawings; the remaining interactive needs are primarily accessibility-oriented keyboard and focus behavior around navigation and linked controls.
